entities.summary: James Lind was a Scottish physician. He was a pioneer of naval hygiene in the Royal Navy. By conducting one of the first ever clinical trials, he developed the theory that citrus fruits cured scurvy. Lind served in the Royal Navy and then went onto private practice. In 1758 he was appointed chief physician of the Royal Naval Hospital Haslar, then one of the largest hospitals in the world. While chief physician, Lind argued for the health benefits of better ventilation aboard naval ships, the improved cleanliness of sailors' bodies, clothing and bedding, and below-deck fumigation with sulphur and arsenic.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Lind's work on naval hygiene led to significant improvements in sailor health and survival rates, with estimates suggesting a 50% reduction in scurvy-related deaths. His advocacy for better ventilation and sanitation practices had far-reaching implications for the development of modern naval medicine.
